title: Temple I at Tikal (Temple of the Great Jaguar)
summary: Temple I is a nine-terraced Maya pyramid on the Great Plaza at Tikal in Guatemala, built about 700 CE and standing roughly 145 feet high. Excavation found a rich burial beneath it, linked to the Late Classic ruler Jasaw Chan K'awiil. It faces Temple II across the plaza and is among Tikal's best-known buildings.

uncertainty.note: Start is 'about the year A.D. 700' (Penn Museum, Expedition magazine). The same project places the death of the ruler linked to the temple at about AD 722. End is the present: the temple stands.

as_recorded.value: was built about the year A.D. 700

importance.justification: The best-known building at Tikal, a UNESCO World Heritage site, and a model of the Late Classic Maya temple-pyramid.
